work_order.understanding:
A custom report appends three synthetic rows — Uncategorized (uncategorized_id 'other'), Transfers ('transfer') and Off budget ('off_budget') — declared in categoryLists() at packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/ReportOptions.ts:348, :354 and :360, each with `id: ''`, and parks them under the synthetic 'Uncategorized & Off budget' group (ReportOptions.ts:375-381) that categoryLists appends to categoryGroup at :404-407. That group is the only one whose members are not keyed by a uuid.

The duplicate-key warning comes from exactly one render site. With Mode=Total, Viz=Data Table and the default Group by=Category, ReportTableList takes the grouped branch (ReportTableList.tsx:28-30, data.groupedData) and renders each group's members at ReportTableList.tsx:73-87 with key={category.id} (line 77). The uncategorized group therefore emits three sibling keys of '' on every render and React logs 'Encountered two children with the same key'. 'Show empty rows' is what makes it unconditional: without it filterEmptyRows (filterEmptyRows.ts:16-24) drops synthetic rows whose amount is zero, so the keys only collide when at least two of the three survive. With it on, filterEmptyRows returns true unconditionally (its line 24, `return !showEmpty ? showHide : true`), so all three always render and all three keys always collide.

Two neighbouring key={item.id} / key={category.id} uses look like candidates and are not. ReportTableRow.tsx:97 puts the key on the single element that component returns, which is never an array child (RenderTableRow.tsx:34-44 renders it singly), so React ignores it. ReportTableList.tsx:55 and ReportTableHeader.tsx:87 key by index. CategorySelector.tsx:226 keys by id, but ReportSidebar.tsx:701-704 feeds it categories.grouped.filter(...) straight off useCategories() — never categoryLists()' output — so the synthetic group never reaches it.

This is a one-line fix and it changes nothing a person can see. I could not execute anything to confirm the warning: this checkout has no node_modules in either the root or packages/desktop-client, so no test or build runs. The claim rests on reading a closed set — three declared id: '' values and the one key={category.id} that consumes exactly those three members.
work_order.root_cause: Three distinct report rows share one entity id (id: ''), and ReportTableList keys its sibling rows by that id, so three siblings collide on every render of the Category-grouped Data Table with 'Show empty rows' on.
work_order.approach:
Change the key at the render site; do not touch the three entity identities. This is what the ticket asks for, and reading the code says it is also the only safe place to change it — id: '' is load-bearing downstream in ways a distinct id would silently break.

The check I ran for each candidate lookup that matches on id:

- filterHiddenItems.ts discriminates the three rows on item.uncategorized_id, not id — unaffected either way.
- recalculate.ts and custom-spreadsheet.ts:212-235 match a row with asset[groupByLabel] === (item.id ?? null) || (item.uncategorized_id && groupsByCategory). With id '' the first clause is false and the second carries the row; a distinct id would make the first clause false too, so amounts would not move.
- narrowCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts:126-166) builds its keep-set from the real category list and runs before categoryLists() appends the synthetic rows, so the synthetic block is never narrowed away. An existing test already pins this (custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:650-666).
- calculateLegend.ts:70-73 sets dataKey: item.id || item.name and custom-spreadsheet.ts:277 sets stacked[item.id || item.name] from the same expression, so giving the rows real ids would move both together — a wide, chart-visible change for no benefit here.
- showActivity.ts:73-79 is the one that decides it. For the Uncategorized row the drilldown passes field: 'category', id: '', uncategorizedId: 'other'; `id && {...}` is falsy on the empty string, so no category condition is emitted. Give the row id: 'uncategorized' and the same click emits category is 'uncategorized', a filter that matches no category and turns the row's drilldown into an empty result — a behaviour change in the opposite direction from the ticket's goal.
- CategorySelector never sees these rows, so changing ids would not have broken its checkbox matching either — but it would have put a lie in the code for the next reader.

So: one line. At ReportTableList.tsx:77 replace key={category.id} with a key derived from the field that actually distinguishes these rows. recalculate (recalculate.ts:127) already copies uncategorized_id onto every row as uncategorizedId, and the type carries it (GroupedEntity, packages/loot-core/src/types/models/reports.ts:117), so the render site has what it needs without touching ReportOptions.ts:

    key={category.uncategorizedId ?? category.id}

For the three synthetic rows this yields 'other', 'transfer', 'off_budget'; for every real category uncategorizedId is undefined and the key stays the uuid it is today, so no existing row's key changes. Real category ids are uuids, so none can equal 'other'/'transfer'/'off_budget', and the three members live in a group with no real members, so the keys are distinct within the sibling list. Add a comment at that line saying why.

What this deliberately does not touch: the row values, the amounts, the group, the sidebar, the legend, and the graph dataKeys.

Reconciliation note: changing the key changes which DOM node React reuses for these three rows. ReportTableRow holds no per-row state, so there is nothing to leak between rows, and the change is in the direction of React doing the right thing — under duplicate keys it was already reusing the wrong nodes.

One surface, both faces planned here: the one-line code change plus a vitest file that renders ReportTableList directly with a fixture carrying the three synthetic rows and asserts no duplicate-key console.error, three distinct keys, and all three names present.

**Answering the recorded objection, which is correct and is answered by editing AC-4 and AC-3 — the only two criteria that pinned generated data.**

(1) AC-4's how_to_verify pinned the literal chip string 'category one of [Cell, Internet, Mortgage, 2 more items...]'. I confirmed the reviewer is right that this is unproducible, and traced it further than the objection did. The chip is ConditionsOpMenu/AppliedFilters -> FilterExpression.tsx:89-91 -> ConditionExpression.tsx:51-52 -> Value.tsx:144-200. `oneOf` renders as t('one of') (packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.ts:81-82) and the field label is t('category') (rule.ts:57-58), so the prefix is stable. The bracketed names are not: Value.tsx:155-157 truncates to `value.slice(0, 3)` whenever the array is longer than four, and the order is the order of `newCategories.map(({ id }) => id)` in CustomReport.tsx:219-230 — i.e. the order categories were clicked, which for a QA-provisioned fixture set is whatever QA created and in whatever order. The demo budget's Bills group yields Power, Water, Mortgage, Internet, Cell in sort_order (mocks/budget.ts:818-828, server/db/index.ts:345-346), so even against the demo budget the chip would read '[Power, Water, Mortgage, 2 more items...]'. AC-4 now asserts the invariant — the chip begins 'category one of', every name it shows is a real category QA created itself, and none of them is 'Uncategorized', 'Transfers' or 'Off budget' — and the second half uses the observable the reviewer named: the report still fetches and re-renders its amounts when the filter is applied and cleared. The demo-budget fixture names are gone from the procedure.

(2) Re-reading AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 and AC-5 for the same defect class, as asked, found one more instance the review had read as clean, so AC-4 does not end up the only edit. AC-3's how_to_verify said 'click "Unselect All", then check the Bills group checkbox'. 'Bills' is a demo-budget category group (mocks/budget.ts:818) and .sdlc/agents/qa.md:118-120 requires QA to provision its own fixtures, so on a QA-provisioned budget there may be no group named 'Bills' at all and the step is unfollowable. It is the same defect: a generated-data name as an exact expectation. AC-3 now says to check whatever category group QA's own fixture data contains, read from the sidebar as rendered, and asserts only presence and absence. qa_script step 6 was rewritten to match. The rest of the re-read found nothing: AC-1 pins no data value (only UI labels, all of which I verified exist in source — 'Data Table' is the button title at ReportTopbar.tsx:97, 'Show empty rows' is ReportSidebar.tsx:494, 'Unselect All' is CategorySelector.tsx:133, 'Bar Graph' is ReportTopbar.tsx:108); AC-2 pins only the three synthetic row names, which are product strings from ReportOptions.ts and are correct in any run; AC-5 is a unit test with a fixture the test itself builds.

**Both prior rejections' substance is retained.** v2 had already answered the two objections of the round before it, and I re-verified those answers against the repo rather than taking them on trust: .sdlc/config.yml:172 really does set `e2e: ""` and .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml:245-252 really does print 'verify.e2e not configured - skipping' and exit 0, so no CI job runs Playwright; packages/desktop-client/vite.config.mts:406 really does scope vitest to `src/**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` with `environment: 'jsdom'`, so a new file under src/ is executed by `yarn test`; and .sdlc/agents/qa.md:152 really does fail a case that 'passed' while throwing console errors, which is what makes AC-1 provable by QA. No e2e file and no e2e acceptance criterion appears in this plan.

No forbidden path is touched: the change is one source file plus one new test file, both under packages/desktop-client/src/. The earlier e2e entry and its acceptance criterion are absent precisely because covering them would have required editing .sdlc/config.yml, which is forbidden (.sdlc/config.yml:220).

out_of_scope: ReportTableRow.tsx:97 `key={item.id}` is inert — it sits on the single element the component returns, which is never an array child (RenderTableRow.tsx:34-44), so React ignores it and it cannot warn. Worth deleting as a trap for the next reader, but it is not this bug.

The three synthetic rows each render a DOM element with id="" (ReportTableRow.tsx:110, id={totalScrollRef ? 'total' : item.id}), so the table carries three empty id attributes. That is an HTML validity wart, not a React key warning and not console noise. Fixing it means threading an identity helper into the DOM id, which changes ids QA selectors could rely on — its own ticket.

ReportTableList.tsx:55 keys the group rows by array index, so reordering the groups makes React reuse the wrong rows. Index keys do not warn and the rows hold no state, so this is latent rather than active — a real reconciliation bug, and a separate change.

The three synthetic rows' drilldown emits no category filter at all (showActivity.ts:73-79, `id && ...` falsy on ''), so clicking Uncategorized's amount shows unfiltered activity. This change deliberately preserves it; changing it is a product decision about what those rows should drill into, not a key fix.

CategorySelector.tsx:226 keys and matches on category.id. The report sidebar never passes it the synthetic group, so it is correct today. It becomes a duplicate-key site only if someone starts feeding it categoryLists() output — noted so that change is not made blind.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `id: ''` is load-bearing. showActivity.ts:73-79 gates the drilldown's category condition on `id &&`, so a truthy id makes clicking the Uncategorized amount emit `category is 'uncategorized'` — a filter matching no category, turning that row's drilldown into an empty result. It also moves calculateLegend.ts:70-73's dataKey and custom-spreadsheet.ts:277's stacked index, a chart-visible change. The ticket explicitly prefers the render site.

alternatives_considered.approach: Key by `${category.uncategorizedId ?? ''}:${category.id}` or another prefixed composite.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: No collision is possible without the prefix, since real ids are uuids and the synthetic members live in a group with no real members. The prefix would be noise that implies a collision the code does not have.

alternatives_considered.approach: Deduplicate at the source in categoryLists() — give the members distinct ids only there.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Same showActivity and legend breakage as giving them real ids; categoryLists() feeds the chart and drilldown paths, not just the table.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep an e2e guard in packages/desktop-client/e2e/ with a verify: "test" criterion citing it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Confirmed in the repo: .sdlc/config.yml:172 leaves verify.e2e empty and .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml:245-252 skips the E2E step with exit 0, while desktop-client's vitest include glob (vite.config.mts:406) excludes e2e/. Nothing would have executed the file, and .sdlc/agents/qa.md:222-224 would then have forced QA to prove a CI-covered criterion from a check that does not exist. The vitest file plus AC-1's browser assertion cover the same ground with runners that exist.

alternatives_considered.approach: Assert the three rows' vertical order in AC-2, as an earlier review's suggested wording put it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: grouped-spreadsheet.ts:193-200 sorts each group's members by amount (sortData.ts:17-49, default sortBy 'desc' on totalDebts), so the order follows the regenerated figures and is not a property this change claims or can deliver. Asserting it would hand QA a criterion the fixed build fails.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep AC-3 naming the demo budget's 'Bills' group, since the objection said AC-4 should end up the only edit.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The objection's defect class is a generated-data name used as an exact expectation, and 'Bills' is exactly that — a demo-budget group (mocks/budget.ts:818) that a run built from QA's own fixtures (.sdlc/agents/qa.md:118-120) need not have, making the step unfollowable. The objection asked for a re-read of AC-1..AC-5 for this class; the re-read found this instance, so editing it follows the instruction rather than contradicting it.

assumptions: The default custom report has Group by=Category (ReportOptions.ts:59, defaultReport), which is what routes ReportTableList into the grouped branch where the duplicate keys occur. If a user's report is grouped by Group, Category+Group, Payee, Account or Interval, the flat branch keys by index at ReportTableList.tsx:55 and the warning does not appear — consistent with the ticket naming the default configuration.

React 19.2.7 (packages/desktop-client/package.json:194) emits 'Encountered two children with the same key' via console.error in its development build. Both the jsdom unit test and QA's dev-server browser rely on that; vitest and `yarn start` both load the development build.
Real category ids are uuids, so no real id can equal 'other', 'transfer' or 'off_budget'. That is what makes `uncategorizedId ?? id` collision-free without a prefix.

The chip's leading text is 'category one of' in QA's run: both strings are product translations (rule.ts:57-58, :81-82) rendered unconditionally, and AC-4 asserts the prefix rather than the names precisely because it is the only stable part.

QA's budget contains at least one category group with at least one category, which AC-3's procedure needs in order to check a group checkbox. If a run's fixtures produced no categories the whole report screen would be empty and no criterion here would be meaningful; that is a fixture problem, not a defect in this change.

No recorded decision constrains this issue: plan/brief.md records nothing under 'Decided for this issue', and the issue body's only instruction-shaped content is the risk note about `id: ''`, which this approach follows.
unknowns: Whether the vitest jsdom render of `ReportTableList` needs the redux/react-query providers. `RenderTableRow` and the `Row` it renders (packages/desktop-client/src/components/table.tsx:288) are presentational, and a stub `renderRow` keeps ReportTableRow — and with it useNavigate, useFormat and useCategories — unmounted, so no provider should be required; wrapping in `TestProviders` from `#mocks` (packages/desktop-client/src/mocks.tsx:42, the wrapper BudgetAnalysisGraph.test.tsx uses) is harmless insurance if the import graph of `#components/table` needs it. Implementer: wrap in TestProviders only if the first render throws.

Whether asserting the three keys directly is possible without reaching into React's internals. If not, the no-duplicate-key assertion plus the distinct `uncategorizedId` values reaching `renderRow` is the achievable form, and the test file should say so.
work_order.debate_summary: No debate — single-agent plan (v3, replanned against the recorded rejection of v2).
residual_risks: The automated guard is a jsdom render of ReportTableList, not the real screen. It proves the three keys no longer collide at the one render site; it does not prove React's reconciliation of the real Data Table (with its header, totals row and interval columns) is warning-free. AC-1 covers that gap in the browser, and the two together are what the ticket asks for.

React could reword the warning; the test matches both /same key/i and the literal React 19 prefix /Encountered two children with the same key/i to survive a rewrite, but a sufficiently different message would need the matcher updated.

AC-3 and AC-4 now describe procedures rather than exact literals, which is what the objection required. That trades a little precision for run-independence: a QA run that mis-clicks a group can still fail these two, but they now fail for a reason in QA's own actions rather than against a string this build never produces.

review.title: The two tests that name key behaviour — 'gives the three synthetic rows three distinct keys' (line 110) and 'keys real category rows by their uuid' (line 144) — assert nothing about keys. Both reduce to the fixture's own contents plus a console filter that only matches duplicate-key wording, so neither fails when the key expression is broken in a different way. The work order names test 3 as 'the regression guard on the `?? category.id` fallback'; it is not one.
review.detail:
The two tests that name key behaviour — 'gives the three synthetic rows three distinct keys' (line 110) and 'keys real category rows by their uuid' (line 144) — assert nothing about keys. Both reduce to the fixture's own contents plus a console filter that only matches duplicate-key wording, so neither fails when the key expression is broken in a different way. The work order names test 3 as 'the regression guard on the `?? category.id` fallback'; it is not one.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/graphs/tableGraph/ReportTableList.test.tsx:144`

Evidence: Mutation run. Replacing ReportTableList.tsx:84 with `key={category.uncategorizedId}` — deleting the `?? category.id` fallback — still passes all 4 tests: `yarn workspace @actual-app/web vitest --run ReportTableList` reports '✓ ReportTableList.test.tsx (4 tests) 46ms / Tests 4 passed (4)'. Every real category row then gets `key={undefined}`, and React's warning for that is a different string than the one the filter looks for. Captured console.error from a scratch render of two uuid-keyed real categories under that mutant: COUNT=1, 'MSG: Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop.%s%s See https://react.dev/link/warning-keys ... Check the render method of `View`. It was passed a child from ReportTableList.' DUPLICATE_KEY_WARNINGS (lines 13-16) is [/same key/i, /Encountered two children with the same key/i], which does not match that string — hence the green run. A regression reintroducing exactly the console noise this ticket exists to remove (one 'unique key' warning per real category on every report render) would ship silently. Test 2 is the same gap in milder form: `syntheticRows.map(item => item.uncategorizedId)` would read 'other'/'transfer'/'off_budget' for any implementation whatsoever, since it reads the fixture rather than the component.

Fix: Make the filter match every React key warning rather than only the duplicate-key phrasing — add /unique .?key.? prop/i (or scope the match to /key/i over React's warning text) so a missing key fails the suite. Test 3 then becomes a real guard on the fallback. Optionally rename test 2 to what it actually checks, or drop it as subsumed by test 1.

review.title: The second entry of DUPLICATE_KEY_WARNINGS is dead: `/Encountered two children with the same key/i` is strictly subsumed by `/same key/i` in the same array, so it can never match a string the first entry rejects. The comment above it states the reason for keeping both — surviving a React rewording of the prefix — which is backwards: the loose entry is the one that survives rewording, and the tight one adds no coverage over it.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/graphs/tableGraph/ReportTableList.test.tsx:13`

Evidence: Every string the tight pattern matches necessarily contains the substring 'same key', so `/same key/i` matches it too. Checked directly: for 'Encountered two children with the same key, `%s`', 'Encountered two children with the same key "a"' and 'Encountered two children with the same key', loose=true and tight=true in all three cases; the implication `tight => loose` holds vacuously for all samples because tight never fires alone. The array reads as two independent safety nets when it is one pattern and a duplicate. The gap that actually matters is the one neither entry covers — React's missing-key wording, 'Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop' — which is reported under my verification of A's finding 0.

Fix: Drop the second entry and rewrite the comment to say what the loose pattern is for: matching any React duplicate-key phrasing rather than pinning React 19's exact sentence, so a reworded prefix does not turn the assertion into a vacuous pass.

review.title: 'does not collide when a real category and a synthetic row are siblings' has no discriminating power over the key expression. Every mutant of ReportTableList.tsx:84 I tried leaves it green, including the unfixed `key={category.id}` — the fixture's uuid `id` and the synthetic row's `id: ''` do not collide under any of them, so the only thing that could fail it is two sibling names colliding, which the fixture does not contain.

'does not collide when a real category and a synthetic row are siblings' has no discriminating power over the key expression. Every mutant of ReportTableList.tsx:84 I tried leaves it green, including the unfixed `key={category.id}` — the fixture's uuid `id` and the synthetic row's `id: ''` do not collide under any of them, so the only thing that could fail it is two sibling names colliding, which the fixture does not contain.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/graphs/tableGraph/ReportTableList.test.tsx:170`

Evidence: Ran four mutants of ReportTableList.tsx:84 against the suite. `key={category.id}` (the pre-fix code) fails tests 1 and 2 but passes tests 3 and 4. `key={category.uncategorizedId}` (fallback deleted), `key={category.name}` and `key={category.uncategorizedId ?? category.id ?? category.name}` all pass all 4. Test 4 is green in every one of those runs, so it constrains nothing about the change it is named after. This is not scope creep — the work order's tests[] asked for this case — and test 2 in the same file does have real value: it fails on the pre-fix code.

Fix: Either delete it, or make it discriminating: give the real category a uuid `id` and assert against a key expression that would collide with it (e.g. a mutant-independent check that the rendered rows carry distinct DOM identity after a re-render). If it stays as a smoke test, rename it so its name stops claiming to guard the key expression.
